# Go Pipeline Framework

This Go module (`github.com/mmaveric/gpf`) provides typed batches, generated
typed nodes, and a graph runtime for batch-oriented pipelines. go.mod declares
Go 1.22; fresh local suites passed on Go 1.22.12 and Go 1.26.8, linux/amd64,
against the same completed source snapshot, not a general Go/OS support promise.
The project is unreleased with target v0.1.0 experimental; API stability is not
promised. Licensing is deferred and remains a publication blocker.

## Project documentation

- [README](README.md): getting started, feature map, ownership, and limitations.
- [Quickstart](examples/quickstart/README.md): runnable finite typed ingress,
  transform, integer sink, and typed error sink; CPU selection and DOT export.
- [Showcase](examples/showcase/README.md): larger order-processing workload.
- [Standalone comparison](examples/standalone-showcase/README.md): comparison
  workload and its current measurement instructions.
- [Fixture generation](examples/testdata/README.md): optional deterministic JSON,
  explicit output paths, no overwrite; ordinary tests do not need these files.
- [Specification guide](spec/README.md): reading map and cross-cutting contracts.
- [Planning and performance spec](spec/05-planning-performance.md): includes
  inactive NUMA metadata and future placement activation gates.
- [Contributing](CONTRIBUTING.md): local development and verification commands.
- [Release preparation](RELEASE.md): support evidence, pending checks, licensing,
  API-stability decisions, and publication gates; not release authorization.
- [Changelog](CHANGELOG.md): unreleased user-visible changes and baseline.
- [Go module](go.mod): module path and minimum Go version.

## Main packages

- `batch`: typed batches and their pools.
- `node`: generated typed node and output contracts.
- `graph`: graph construction, validation, planning, and execution.
- `queue`: bounded concurrent queue implementations.
- `numa`: placement metadata types.
- `runtime`: runtime support types.

For API details, see package documentation, specifications, and source. NUMA
metadata and allocator descriptors are inactive. DrainContext cancellation is
cooperative, not a hard interruption of callbacks. There is no panic recovery.
Open [conformance gates](RELEASE.md#conformance-review-gates) distinguish current
limitations from intended guarantees; passing tests do not resolve them.

From the repository root, run `go run ./examples/quickstart` to begin and
`go test ./...` to test. Consult CONTRIBUTING.md for fresh/race verification;
also run `go test -count=1 ./examples/testdata/generate` explicitly because
`./...` skips testdata. Do not turn a cross-build into a runtime-platform claim.
